title: Mercimek Koftesi
subtitle: Turkish red lentil and bulgur patties
excerpt: Red lentils cooked soft and mixed with fine bulgur, onion, and warm spices, then shaped into small patties. A simple vegan street food that is both filling and bright with lemon.
sourceNotes: Turkish vegan street food and home cooking tradition. Synthesised from multiple Turkish culinary sources.

recipe.batchNotes: Easily doubled. The shaped patties keep in the fridge for up to 2 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The mixture can be made a day ahead. Shape the patties just before serving.

content.text: Mercimek koftesi uses cooked red lentils and bulgur wheat as the base. The heat from the lentils softens the bulgur while it rests, so timing the rest correctly is the key step. The patties should be smooth and hold together cleanly.

Put the lentils and water in the saucepan. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook for 12 minutes until the lentils are completely soft and have absorbed most of the water. The mixture should be thick.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the bulgur wheat straight away. Cover with a lid and leave for 15 minutes. The bulgur will absorb the remaining liquid and steam.

While the bulgur rests, fry the onion in 2 tablespoons of olive oil over a medium heat for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Add the tomato puree, paprika-sweet, paprika-hot, and cumin. Stir for 1 minute. Remove from the heat.
Tip the onion mixture into the lentil and bulgur bowl. Add the remaining olive oil, salt, lemon juice, spring onion, parsley, and mint. Mix well.
Leave the mixture to cool for a further 5 minutes so it is warm but handleable. Taste and adjust salt and lemon.
Take walnut-sized portions and press each one in your palm to form a smooth oval patty. Make a shallow indent down the length with your finger if you like the traditional shape.
Arrange on a plate and serve with lemon wedges. Scatter with sumac if using.

items.symptom: The patties do not hold together.
items.cause: The lentils were too wet, or the bulgur did not absorb fully.
items.fix: Rest the mixture a further 10 minutes. If still too wet, add another 2 tablespoons of bulgur and mix through.

items.symptom: The mixture is dry and stiff.
items.cause: The lentils cooked with too little water, or the bulgur absorbed too much.
items.fix: Stir in a tablespoon of olive oil and a squeeze of lemon to loosen the texture.

items.cause: Not enough salt, lemon, or spice.
items.fix: Taste the mixture before shaping. Adjust with more salt, lemon juice, and a pinch of paprika-hot.
